# Case: intent

Version 1.0.0 of the specification: why the system is built and what counts as success, the problem, 1 goal, 1 out-of-scope entry and 2 quality goals, in the shape of section 1 of arc42. Every other part of the specification is judged against this page.

## 1. Problem

Clerks cannot find an item by name, so a sale waits while they search.

Who it hurts: clerk.

Today: A search takes 90 seconds on average (March 2026).

## 2. Goals

The outcomes the owner of the system wants, each with what is counted, the value today and the value wanted, and the needs that serve it.

| Goal | Statement | Measure | Baseline | Target | By | Priority | Status | Served by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GOAL-1 | Sales wait less. | Seconds from request to counter. | 90 seconds | 20 seconds |   | must | accepted | NEED-1 |

## 3. Out of scope

What the system will not do, decided on purpose, so a question or a change request that asks for it is answered here.

| Entry | Statement | Until | Rules out |
|---|---|---|---|
| OUT-1 | The system does not order stock. | not planned |   |

**Insight on OUT-1:** Ordering belongs to the warehouse system.

## 4. Quality goals

The qualities that matter most, in rank order: when two pull apart, the higher rank wins.

| Rank | Quality goal | Quality | Statement | Requirements |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | QG-1 | functional-suitability | A name search finds every item of that name. | CASE-1 |
| 2 | QG-2 | interaction-capability | A clerk finds an item in under ten seconds. |   |
